opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin on Source Code. Full-time employees max is write unless their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code, so admin is not permitted. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training, never admin). Since admin is requested but not permitted, recommend granting read.
reason: Alexandra Johnson (E003) requested admin on Source Code. Admin is not permitted in either interpretation: as a full-time Analyst, the maximum is write (admin only if the role owns the system, and Analyst does not own Source Code); as a contractor with basic security training, the maximum is read and admin is never allowed. Because the HR and Security notes conflict on employment type, I grant the most restrictive level that is safe under both readings: read.
